speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo. To help me determine the cause, can you describe the sensation in more detail? Specifically, does the room feel like it is spinning around you, or do you feel unsteady and lightheaded?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. Does changing your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up, trigger or worsen the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you currently have any hearing loss, ringing in the ears (tinnitus), or a feeling of fullness in either ear? I also need to know if you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or recent head trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of auditory symptoms and cardiovascular risk factors, combined with the brief, position-related nature of the vertigo, strongly suggests Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). To confirm this, I need to see if specific head movements reproduce the vertigo and nystagmus. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver on the left side, combined with the brief, position-triggered vertigo and absence of other neurological or auditory symptoms, confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
